title: NVFP4 paged KV on the fork's DFlash2 port on the RTX 5090: two requests start with four device state slots and 262,144 KV tokens, rounds are 12-27% shorter behind 32K-120K tokens and unchanged at short context, the durable store keeps exact restores and shipped v0.9.0's reuse, and MTP3 stays byte-identical
question: EXP-080 measured upstream's NVFP4 KV under DFlash2: two requests start with four device state slots and 262,144 KV tokens at no measured speed cost. EXP-083 showed the fork's BF16 two-slot DFlash2 profile keeps the durable store but re-prefills a sibling under device-state pressure that shipped's four slots serve from an anchor. Ported onto the fork with every BF16, INT8 and FP8 path unchanged, does NVFP4 KV give the fork's DFlash2 profile four slots and at least 262,144 KV tokens, at no more than 3% round cost, with the durable store intact and MTP3 byte-identical?
answer: Yes. With NVFP4 KV the two-request DFlash2 profile started with --device-state-slots 4 and resolved 262,144 KV tokens (BF16 on the same binary: 131,520; shipped v0.9.0: 160,256). The KV payload fell from 8.03 GiB to 4.50 GiB while doubling capacity, VRAM in use after the decode probe from 29,470 to 26,232 MiB, and 5.07 GiB stayed free after startup against 1.91 GiB. Rounds matched BF16 at short context (15.55 vs 15.57 ms) and in the pair (23.0-23.2 vs 23.0-23.3 ms) and were 12%, 19% and 27% shorter behind 32K, 64K and 120K tokens (18.82 vs 25.89 ms at 120K). The durable sequence passed with shipped's reuse pattern: a 57,889-token session restored hot after two restarts (214 and 236 tokens computed) from a 1.66 GB checkpoint saved in 1.56 s (BF16 DFlash2: 4.41 GB, 3.29 s), the sibling probe reused on the same four steps as shipped v0.9.0 (EXP-083's two-slot profile had re-prefilled sibling_2), and the multi-session probe lost no reuse (shipped: 2 of 12). MTP3 on the binary stayed 89/89 byte-identical to v0.9.0 and v0.8.7. One unpowered role-corpus run of the NVFP4 profile decoded 24.0% faster than MTP3 in the same window, and its evidence precision was 0.951 against MTP3's 0.994, a gap larger than the automatic-use gate's 2.0 points.

decision.action: keep NVFP4 as the DFlash2 port's KV format; next, a powered quality screen of the DFlash2 NVFP4 profile against shipped MTP3
decision.rule: Pre-registered before the window (PLAN.md): keep if (a) every listed GPU test passes; (b) the NVFP4 arm starts at two requests with --device-state-slots 4 and resolves at least 262,144 KV tokens; (c) on each probe step (contexts 0, 32K, 64K, 120K and the pair) the NVFP4 arm's mean ms per round is at most 1.03 x the BF16 arm's in this window; (d) on the NVFP4 arm restore_probe exits 0 with both restored continuations restored (computed_prefill_tokens <= 1,024), multisession reuse_lost <= 2 (shipped v0.9.0's on the identical sequence, EXP-083), the sibling probe reuses on shipped's steps (cached tokens > 0 on depth_1, sibling_1, sibling_2 and continue_sibling_2), no server error and no refused export; (e) spk5-mtp3-c1 answers 89/89 byte-identically to shipped v0.9.0 and v0.8.7. Reject on any failure; diagnose the failing stage and rerun it.

rule_outcome.a_gpu_tests: pass after one rerun: in the first window 7 of 9 invocations passed and both attention invocations aborted on a test defect (see gpu_tests); after a test-only fix the second window ran both attention invocations and both passed, including every legacy BF16, INT8 and FP8 attention case
rule_outcome.b_capacity: pass: 262,144 KV tokens (4,096 of 4,096 pages) with --max-concurrency 2 and --device-state-slots 4
rule_outcome.c_round_cost: pass: NVFP4/BF16 ms per round 0.999 at context 0, 0.881 at 32K, 0.809 at 64K, 0.727 at 120K, 1.010 and 0.988 for the pair; maximum 1.010 against the 1.03 bound
rule_outcome.d_durable: pass: restore_probe exit 0, restored continuations computed 214 and 236 tokens; sibling cached tokens 81, 116, 61 and 155 on the four steps (shipped: 81, 116, 61, 155); multisession reuse_lost 0 of 12; 0 server errors, 0 request errors, 0 frontier refusals, every shutdown 'refused 0'
rule_outcome.e_mtp3_identity: pass: 89/89 against v0.9.0 (pub-v0614b1) and 89/89 against v0.8.7 (pub-v0613b1)

decision.reason: Every criterion held. NVFP4 returns the capacity DFlash2's weights took from the two-request profile and more (262,144 tokens with four slots against shipped's 160,256 with four), costs nothing at short context and in the pair, and shortens long-context rounds because each verify reads 3.6 times fewer KV bytes. With four slots the planner served the sibling EXP-083's two-slot profile re-prefilled, and the multi-session probe kept every reuse.
decision.not_decided_here: Adoption. The NVFP4 profile's outputs differ from shipped's in 79 of 89 role-corpus cases, and its single run's evidence precision (0.951 against 0.994) is outside the automatic-use gate's 2.0-point criterion. One run per arm cannot tell that from prompt-level noise; EXP-080's upstream NVFP4 run measured 0.979 against its BF16 run's 0.993.
decision.next: EXP-085: a pre-registered, powered paired quality screen of the role corpus under non-semantic prompt variants (EXP-063's method extended to every primary gate metric): shipped v0.9.0 MTP3 against the DFlash2 K=7 NVFP4 two-request profile, with the BF16 DFlash2 profile as a second candidate to separate NVFP4's effect from DFlash2's.

limits: Criterion (a) passed only after the attention tests were rerun in a second window. The fix touched the test source only; the server binary used by every arm is the one built before the first window, and the rerun covered the two attention invocations, not the other seven, which had passed.

One run per arm and probe on one appliance. The decode probe's prompts carry random nonces, so the two DFlash2 arms decoded different texts; ms per round is the comparable measure, and tok/s and tokens per round move with the text.

The role-corpus quality figures are one unpowered run per arm. The NVFP4 profile's evidence precision (0.951 against 0.994) and its 79 of 89 changed outputs are the open quality question, not a measured regression.
The NVFP4 arm ran with the durable store on and the BF16 arm without it; the decode probe saves no checkpoint (its server's shutdown reported saved 0, nothing to save 0).
Durability and reuse were measured on the NVFP4 arm only in this window; the shipped and BF16 two-slot comparisons are EXP-083's runs of the identical sequence on the same appliance.

The spike binary is an incremental archive build (source_dirty=true) of a branch, not a release candidate. No sm_89 or sm_86 build was made; those lanes compile the NVFP4 launchers as rejecting stubs.
